category.title: Shoulders
category.intro: Programmes that strengthen the shoulder muscles and protect the small muscles that wrap the shoulder from the inside (the rotator cuff) and control the shoulder blade. You start with warm-up moves and progress to pike push-ups and the wall handstand.
science: The pike push-up shifts the load from the chest to the shoulders; building strength first with normal and incline push-ups is recommended.
The scapular push-up (push-up plus) is one of the moves that work the serratus most, the muscle that holds the shoulder blade against the ribcage; it's important for shoulder health.
Adding light external rotation and shoulder-blade work to the warm-up is widely recommended; it isn't proven to prevent injury, but it's considered harmless and useful.
Don't force overhead moves when your shoulder hurts; work within a pain-free range.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.setup: Stand tall and open your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
steps: Draw small circles with your arms.
Slowly make the circles bigger.
Change direction halfway through.
exercises.tip: Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
exercises.mistake: Don't swing them fast and jerkily; keep the movement controlled.

exercises.name: Wall Slide
exercises.setup: Lean your back against a wall and raise your arms like goalposts; elbows and backs of your hands on the wall.
steps: Slide your arms up while keeping them on the wall.
Reach as high as is comfortable.
Pull your shoulder blades down to return to the start.
exercises.tip: If your lower back comes off the wall, raise your arms less.
exercises.mistake: Don't hunch your shoulders towards your ears.

exercises.name: Scapular Push-Up
exercises.setup: Get into a push-up position; your arms stay straight.
steps: Without bending your arms, let your chest sink a little; your shoulder blades move together.
Push the floor away and round your upper back towards the ceiling; your shoulder blades spread apart.
Repeat this small movement in rhythm.
exercises.tip: If it's too hard, do it with your knees on the floor.
exercises.mistake: Don't bend your elbows; the movement comes only from your shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.setup: From a push-up position, lift your hips up; your body forms an upside-down V. Hands shoulder-width apart.
steps: Bend your elbows to bring your head towards the floor slightly in front of your hands.
Stop when your head nears the floor.
Push back up to straighten your arms.
exercises.tip: The closer your feet are to your hands, the harder the move.
exercises.mistake: Don't flare your elbows straight out; let them bend slightly backwards.

exercises.name: Elevated Pike Push-Up
exercises.setup: Put your feet on a sturdy chair or step and your hands on the floor; hips up, body as upright as possible.
steps: Bend your elbows to bring your head towards the floor.
Hold steady.
Push back up.
exercises.tip: It's the next step on the road to the handstand push-up.
exercises.mistake: Don't bump your head on the floor; keep the lowering slow.

exercises.name: Pike Hold
exercises.setup: Hands and feet on the floor, hips up high; your body like an upside-down V.
steps: Push the floor away to move your shoulders away from your ears.
Keep your hips up.
Keep breathing and hold.
exercises.tip: You can bend your knees slightly; keep your back straight.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your shoulders sink; keep pushing the floor away with your arms.

exercises.name: Down Dog to Plank
exercises.setup: Start in an upside-down V position: hips up, hands and feet on the floor.
steps: Lower your hips and bring your shoulders over your hands to move into a plank.
Pause briefly in the plank.
Push your hips back up to return to the V.
exercises.tip: Your hands and feet stay where they are.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your hips sag in the plank.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.setup: Get into a push-up position; spread your feet a little to make balancing easier.
steps: Touch your left shoulder with your right hand.
Put your hand down and touch your right shoulder with your left hand.
Keep alternating without rocking your hips.
exercises.tip: If it's too hard, put your knees down.
exercises.mistake: Don't rock your hips sideways with each tap.

exercises.name: Bear Hold
exercises.setup: Get on all fours: hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips. Tuck your toes.
steps: Lift your knees 2–3 centimetres off the floor.
Keep your back flat and your shoulders over your hands.
Keep breathing and hold.
exercises.tip: Keep your knees close to the floor; don't lift them high.
exercises.mistake: Don't lift your hips or let your back sag.

exercises.name: Reverse Tabletop
exercises.target: Back of the shoulders, back and glutes
exercises.setup: Sit on the floor, bend your knees and put your hands on the floor behind your hips; fingers pointing towards your feet.
steps: Push through your palms and heels to lift your hips; your body and thighs should be flat like a table.
Pause briefly at the top and open your chest.
Lower your hips slowly.
exercises.tip: If your wrists strain, turn your fingers to the side.
exercises.mistake: Don't let your shoulders sink towards your ears.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
exercises.target: Rotator cuff (the muscles that wrap the shoulder from the inside)
exercises.setup: Lie on your side with your head on your lower arm. Bend your top elbow to 90 degrees and rest it against your waist, hand in front of your belly.
steps: Keeping your elbow at your waist, rotate your forearm up towards the ceiling.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly; switch sides halfway through.
exercises.tip: Tucking a small towel under your armpit keeps your elbow in place.
exercises.mistake: Don't lift your elbow off your body; the movement comes only from the forearm.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
exercises.target: Lower trapezius and back of the shoulders
exercises.setup: Lie face down. Stretch your arms overhead in a Y shape, thumbs pointing up.
steps: Lift your arms off the floor; pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Hold for a moment at the top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Your chest may lift slightly; the main movement comes from the arms.
exercises.mistake: Don't hunch your shoulders towards your ears.

exercises.name: Prone T Raise
exercises.target: Back of the shoulders and middle trapezius
exercises.setup: Lie face down and open your arms out to the sides in a T shape.
steps: Keeping your arms straight, lift them up from the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold briefly.
Lower slowly.
exercises.tip: Turning your thumbs up makes it easier on the shoulder.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
exercises.setup: Back to the wall, hands on the floor one and a half steps from it. Put your feet on the wall and slowly walk them up.
steps: Walk your feet up the wall until your hips are above your shoulders.
Keep your arms straight and hold, pushing the floor away.
Come down by slowly walking your feet down.
exercises.tip: Only try it if pike push-ups feel easy; increase the height gradually.
exercises.mistake: If you feel dizzy or your shoulder hurts, come down right away.
